"Hey." A woman, maybe 30s, with thick glasses settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 30s, with thick glasses.)

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.

A person, maybe 60s and A man, maybe 30s, with a crooked nose are comparing scars like trading cards.

A woman, maybe 30s, with thick glasses is hurt — a fall, a thorn, a bad step. (health 84/100)

Fresh-cut stems on the north ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Thornfield's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)
